Discovered from pm-gh1647 during the PR 1648 CodeRabbit review (two Major and two Minor follow-ups, all present at the merge base before pm-gh1647).

pm-gh1647 refuses a lock directory that is ALREADY a symlink or non-directory, and detects a swap between its confinement check and `open(wx)` by comparing dev/ino identity. Every later step still acts by pathname, so a concurrent writer that swaps `locks/` (or a parent) for a symlink in the window can make pm act outside the tracker:

1. **`pm gc --scope locks` sweep** (`src/core/lock/lock-gc.ts`): `inspectConfinedLockDirectory` runs once before `readdir`. The per-entry `readFile`, the cleanup gate in `removeObservedLock` and `fs.unlink(lockPath)` all re-resolve the path. A mid-scan swap can unlink an expired `*.lock` in an outside directory and report it as `locks/<file>`.
2. **Post-EEXIST stale reclaim** (`src/core/lock/lock.ts`, acquire loop): after `EEXIST`, `assertLockCreateContention` checks only that the final entry is not a symlink. The reclaim then reads `lockPath`, takes the stale cleanup gate and unlinks `lockPath` by pathname. If the directory was swapped before `open(wx)`, `EEXIST` can come from an outside `<id>.lock`, and a stale or dead-owner outside file can be deleted.
3. **Post-create entry check** (`verifyConfinedLockCreation`): the directory identity is re-inspected by pathname and then `lstat(lockPath)` runs separately. A swap between the two calls to an outside directory that holds a hard link to the created inode passes the identity check. The returned lease then releases and fences by pathname.
4. **lstat failure treated as absent** (`assertLockEntryNotSymlink`): every lstat error returns early, so a transient non-ENOENT failure after `EEXIST` lets `readLockInfo` read the entry with a symlink-following `readFile`. Windows `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY` delete-pending waits (recognized by `isLockCreateContention`) must keep waiting rather than become failures.

Threat model: a pre-existing symlink committed into a cloned repository is already refused by pm-gh1647. These windows need a concurrent local writer that can modify `.agents/pm/` while pm runs, which is the same actor that could edit items directly, so the impact is narrower. It still contradicts the documented confinement guarantee.

Approach: Node has no `openat` / `unlinkat`. On Linux, open the verified directory with `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW` and address entries through `/proc/self/fd/<dirfd>/<name>`; the magic link stays bound to the verified directory inode even if the path is swapped. This gives `*at` semantics for read, gate creation and unlink. Elsewhere, re-verify the directory identity immediately before each destructive step and refuse to reclaim or sweep (typed `lock_path_unsafe` / `lock_directory_replaced`) when it no longer matches the identity observed at the start, rather than proceeding by pathname.
Lock GC sweep, stale-lock reclaim and the post-create entry check act by pathname after a one-time confinement check, so a mid-operation lock-directory swap can reach outside the tracker

pm gc --scope locks never unlinks or reads a lock entry outside the tracker when locks/ is swapped for a symlink during the sweep, proven by a regression test that swaps the directory between readdir and removal; The post-EEXIST stale-lock reclaim never reads, gates or unlinks through a replaced lock directory and refuses with lock_path_unsafe when the directory identity changed since creation, proven by a swap regression test; verifyConfinedLockCreation binds its entry check to the verified directory (Linux procfs dirfd) so a hard-linked inode in a swapped outside directory cannot pass, and other platforms refuse when identity cannot be bound; assertLockEntryNotSymlink treats only ENOENT as absent while preserving the Windows EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY delete-pending waits; docs/SDK.md states the exact confinement guarantee per operation and platform

Every destructive lock step (gc sweep unlink, stale reclaim read/gate/unlink, lease release) stays bound to the lock directory identity verified at the start, or refuses with lock_path_unsafe when that identity no longer holds
Only the initial lock-directory check and the post-create identity comparison are confined. Later reads, gates and unlinks re-resolve the pathname and follow a directory swapped mid-operation

Lock GC sweep, post-EEXIST stale reclaim and the post-create entry check re-resolve lock paths after pm-gh1647's one-time confinement check, so a concurrent lock-directory swap can make pm read or unlink outside the tracker. Bind those steps to the verified directory (Linux procfs dirfd) or refuse when its identity changed.

patch.value: pm gc --scope locks never unlinks or reads a lock entry outside the tracker when locks/ is swapped for a symlink during the sweep, proven by a regression test that swaps the directory between readdir and removal; The post-EEXIST stale-lock reclaim never reads, gates or unlinks through a replaced lock directory and refuses with lock_path_unsafe when the directory identity changed since creation, proven by a swap regression test; verifyConfinedLockCreation binds its entry check to the verified directory (Linux procfs dirfd) so a hard-linked inode in a swapped outside directory cannot pass, and other platforms refuse when identity cannot be bound; assertLockEntryNotSymlink treats only ENOENT as absent while preserving the Windows EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY delete-pending waits; docs/SDK.md states the exact confinement guarantee per operation and platform; When the post-open entry check refuses with lock_path_unsafe after a late swap, the SDK removes the lock file it just created only if that path still names the inode of the opened descriptor (verified through the bound directory, never by a fresh pathname lookup), so no empty lock file is left outside the tracker and no file pm did not create is ever unlinked, proven by the GH-1652 late-swap regression (fs.open mocked to swap locks/ just before the wx open)

message: Extend the post-create confinement scope with the GH-1652 debris-on-refusal case

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: GH-1652 (opened 2026-11-02, reproduced against SDK 2026.11.2 on Node 26) maps here. pm-gh1647's post-open check correctly refuses with lock_path_unsafe when locks/ is swapped for a symlink between the confinement checks and the exclusive open. But the 0-byte <id>.lock that the open created stays in the symlink target, outside the tracker. This is the refusal-side half of the post-create entry seam (body item 3): the cleanup must be bound to the same verified directory and inode identity as the check, or it becomes a pathname unlink outside the tracker. Added as an acceptance criterion instead of filing a separate item, because the fix shares the dirfd binding this item already prescribes. Linux procfs dirfd: unlink only when the opened descriptor's dev/ino still matches the bound entry. Elsewhere: refuse, and report the residue path in the refusal context so the caller can remove it.
